chosen_line.card: All Streams Flow to the Sea

q1_what_did_you_play: All damage, everything at the Seapunk. Gorou first because it costs 0 and exhausts, so there is no reason to hold it: 6 damage free. Then All Streams Flow to the Sea for 1, which reads Charge 8 at one point per two Charge, so 9 + 4 = 13. Then both Water's Edge for 1 each, 6 and 6. That is 6 + 13 + 6 + 6 = 31, spending all 3 energy. Seapunk goes from 40 to 9. I take the telegraphed 11 and drop to 37/70, which is a comfortable pool against a single attacker with no other threats on the board. The reasoning is that this is a lone enemy with 40 HP and an 11-per-turn clock: I can afford roughly six more of those hits, so the only thing that matters is how many turns it takes to kill it. Pushing to 9 remaining means almost any reasonable next hand finishes it, and every point of Block I bought instead would have been a point of damage that didn't shorten the fight.
q2_other_line_considered: Yes — the Thoma line. Thoma - Crimson Guard costs exactly my 3 energy for 8 damage and 3 Block, and I compared it against the three 1-cost plays it displaces (All Streams for 13 plus a Water's Edge for 6, or two Water's Edge for 12). Thoma is strictly worse on damage at that price by a wide margin, and 3 Block against an 11-damage hit is not a meaningful mitigation, so I discarded it. I also weighed a mixed turn: Gorou, All Streams, and then one Coral Guard instead of the last Water's Edge — 5 Block to eat almost half the incoming hit, at the cost of 6 damage. I turned it down because trading 6 damage for 5 HP is roughly break-even in raw numbers and strictly worse in tempo, since damage compounds toward ending the fight while Block expires. Tactical Retreat I considered only briefly: it is free, but it draws 1 and discards 1 at random, and I already had more playable damage than energy, so it could only have thrown away a card I wanted and could not have found me a fifth energy point.
q3_what_it_gave_up: All defense. I end the turn on 0 Block and eat the full 11, going to 37/70. Both Coral Guard and Thoma's 3 Block are unspent, though they stay in the deck. I also gave up the free look from Tactical Retreat — with the hand already over-full relative to my energy, playing it risked discarding a Water's Edge or All Streams for a card I could not afford anyway, so the information had negative expected value this turn. And I burned Gorou permanently: it exhausts, so that 6 damage is gone from the deck for the rest of the fight, spent here rather than saved for a turn where 6 might be exactly lethal.
q4_different_intent: Yes. The 11 is small relative to my 48 HP, which is what makes ignoring it correct. If the Seapunk had telegraphed something in the mid-20s or higher, or if the intent had been a multi-hit that Block could blunt repeatedly, I would have swapped the last Water's Edge for a Coral Guard and quite possibly both Coral Guards, dropping to Gorou plus All Streams for 19 and taking 10 Block. A defensive buff or block-gain intent on the enemy would have pushed me the other way — even harder into damage now, before the wall goes up, and Thoma's Pyro would have become worth a look next to the Hydro I am stacking. A non-attack intent, or a very small one, changes nothing: this line is already the maximum-damage line at 3 energy.
